# EO 14179 — Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence

> **Federal policy, not NASA governance: binding on agencies as federal policy, a separate
> question from what NASA's own directives require.** Useful for comparison and vocabulary.
> It never by itself establishes what a specific NASA directive requires, and must not be
> cited as NASA coverage.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Publisher / owner** | The President (Executive Office of the President) |
| **Kind** | Executive Order |
| **Status** | Signed and effective January 23, 2025; published in the Federal Register January 31, 2025, Vol. 90, No. 20, FR Doc. 2025-02172 [p.1-2]. Cited as 90 FR 8741; that page-number form is cited as reported and was not independently checked. Currently in force; no later rescission of this EO found in the five documents reviewed. |
| **Where to get it** | Federal Register / govinfo.gov, free public (citation 90 FR 8741 — verify). Public copy, confirmed anonymously off-network on 2026-10-26: `https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-31/pdf/2025-02172.pdf` |
| **Binds whom** | Executive Branch agencies generally; specific duties fall on the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology (APST), the Special Advisor for AI and Crypto, the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs (APNSA), the OMB (Office of Management and Budget) Director, and "the heads of such executive departments and agencies... as the APST and APNSA deem relevant" [p.1, Sec. 4(a)] |

**What it is good for, relative to NASA's documents.** (our reading) This is the short policy-framework order that triggered the current federal AI policy stack: it revokes the prior EO and sets the general direction ("global AI dominance," freedom from "ideological bias") that the later OMB memos implement. It is useful for dating when the current federal AI policy regime began and for naming the officials who hold federal AI policy authority — it contains no agency-level practices or technical requirements of its own.

**Key content for artificial intelligence / machine-learning assurance.**
- [p.1] Sec. 2: Policy "to sustain and enhance America's global AI dominance in order to promote human flourishing, economic competitiveness, and national security."
- [p.1] Sec. 3: Adopts the AI definition at 15 U.S.C. 9401(3) by reference rather than defining AI itself.
- [p.1] Sec. 4(a): Directs an AI Action Plan within 180 days of the order, developed by APST, the Special Advisor for AI and Crypto, and APNSA with OMB and relevant agency heads.
- [p.1-2] Sec. 5(a)-(b): Revokes Executive Order 14110 ("Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence") and directs agencies to identify and suspend, revise, or rescind conflicting actions taken under it, including revising OMB Memoranda M-24-10 and M-24-18 within 60 days — the step that produced the OMB M-25-21 and M-25-22 memos covered elsewhere in this set.
- No role assignment regarding a Chief AI Officer, "high-impact AI," or minimum/required risk-management practices was found anywhere in this order (per a text search of the public order); it is a short policy-framework document and leaves those to the OMB memos it set in motion.
- AI touchpoints found by a text search of the public order ("artificial intelligence," "AI," "automat..."): the whole order is about AI by subject, but at the level of national policy and officials' roles rather than any system-level, software, or algorithmic detail — no mention of "machine learning," "autonom...," "neural," or "algorithm" specifically.

**Nearest NASA counterpart.** No direct counterpart on the current NASA document list; federal agency policy and NASA's own internal directives are separate coverage areas (our reading) — the nearest topical neighbor would be NASA-HDBK-2203, the one document on the list that discusses AI/machine-learning assurance broadly, but it answers a different question (what NASA's software engineering guidance addresses vs. what federal AI policy directs agencies to do).
